name: swift-extras-base64
baseline: Foundation base64EncodedString / Data(base64Encoded:) with Swift 5.3 (2020), macOS and Linux
verdict_reason: The 3-4x macOS and 3-10x Linux wins were measured against the 2020 Foundation. In February 2025 the same author merged a faster Swift Base64 into swift-foundation that measured 5x-7.5x faster than the Foundation of that time on 1 MB inputs, so the gap against current Foundation has likely closed; no direct comparison is published.
tier_reason: The performance test source is in the repo and the README states the Intel Core i9 MacBook Pro and Swift 5.3; build flags are not stated.
claimed_speedup: macOS, Swift 5.3: encode 0.66s vs 2.08s (3x), decode 0.54s vs 2.15s (4x). Linux: encode 0.27s vs 1.01s (3x), decode 0.41s vs 5.5s (~10x).
workload: Encoding and decoding the base64 form of bytes 0x00-0xFF one million times
hardware: MacBook Pro 16-inch (late 2019), 2.4 GHz 8-core Intel Core i9
one_liner: Foundation-free Base64 that was 3-10x faster than 2020 Foundation; its author has since brought the approach into Foundation.
how_it_is_fast: It maps bytes to characters and back with Chromium's precomputed lookup tables (from Lemire's fastbase64) in tight loops over unsafe buffers, without Foundation's NSData bridging.
use_it_when: Foundation-free targets (Embedded or minimal Linux images) that need Base64
Toolchains or OS versions whose Foundation predates the 2025 swift-foundation Base64 rewrite
skip_it_when: Current Foundation already uses the same author's faster implementation
caveats: Numbers are from Swift 5.3 on a 2019 Intel Mac; build configuration not stated.
Baseline replaced: swift-foundation PRs #1157 and #1160 (merged February 2025) rewrote Foundation's Base64 in Swift, and October 2026 follow-ups made it faster again.
No line-break handling when decoding or encoding.
tradeoffs: Separate API from Foundation's Data methods

evidence.quote: Tests were run on a MacBook Pro (16-inch, late 2019). Processor: 2.4 GHz 8-Core Intel Core i9.
